categories.desc: From the formal bonjour to the affectionate coucou.
cards: Bonjour !
Hello! / Good morning!
Through the day, to everyone: shopkeepers, bus drivers, neighbours. Skipping it sounds rude. You greet a person once a day; meeting again, it's a joking rebonjour !
Bonjour madame, une baguette, s'il vous plaît.
Good morning, a baguette, please.
Bonsoir !
Good evening!
From late afternoon on, as a greeting. Also a goodbye in the evening: bonsoir et merci !
Bonsoir, on a une table pour deux au nom de Martin.
Good evening, we've got a table for two under Martin.
Salut !
Hi!
Informal: friends, family, colleagues you call tu. Doubles as ‘bye’.
Salut Léa ! Ça fait longtemps !
Hi Léa! It's been ages!
Coucou !
Hiya!
Affectionate, for friends, family and children; common at the start of texts.
Coucou ma puce, t'as passé une bonne journée ?
Hiya sweetheart, did you have a good day?

categories.desc: Asking how someone is, and the usual answers.
cards: Ça va ?
How's it going?
The everyday question; the answer uses the same words: ça va, et toi ? Fuller: comment ça va ?
— Salut, ça va ? — Ça va, et toi ?
— Hi, how's it going? — Fine, and you?
Comment allez-vous ?
How are you?
Formal, with vous. Informal but careful: comment vas-tu ? The reply: je vais bien, merci. Et vous ?
Bonjour docteur, comment allez-vous ?
Good morning, doctor, how are you?
Ça roule ?
All good?
Casual. The answer echoes it: ça roule ! (all good!)
— Ça roule ? — Ça roule, et toi ?
— All good? — All good, you?
Quoi de neuf ?
What's new?
Invites news. Common reply: pas grand-chose (not much).
— Quoi de neuf ? — Pas grand-chose, et toi ?
— What's new? — Not much, and you?
Tranquille.
Chilled. / All quiet.
A relaxed, casual answer: nothing much happening, all fine.
— Ça va, ce week-end ? — Tranquille, je me repose.
— How's the weekend going? — Chilled, I'm resting.
Bof, ça va.
Meh, I'm OK.
Bof is a verbal shrug: not great, not terrible. Often an invitation to ask more: — Bof, ça va. — Qu'est-ce qui se passe ?
— Ça va ? — Bof, ça va. Un peu fatigué.
— How are you? — Meh, OK. A bit tired.

categories.desc: The many ways to say ‘bye’ and ‘see you’.
cards: Au revoir !
Goodbye!
All-purpose and polite: shops, offices, strangers. With friends: salut ! or ciao ! (also spelt tchao).
Merci, au revoir, bonne journée !
Thanks, goodbye, have a nice day!
À bientôt !
See you soon!
Friendly and vague about when. Also in emails to people you'll see again.
C'était super de te voir, à bientôt !
It was great to see you, see you soon!
À plus !
See you later!
Casual; the final s is usually pronounced. In texts: À+ or A+.
Je file, à plus !
I'm off, see you later!
À tout à l'heure !
See you in a bit!
When you'll meet again the same day. Casual short form: à toute !
Je vais faire les courses, à tout à l'heure !
I'm going shopping, see you in a bit!
À demain !
See you tomorrow!
À + the time: à lundi !, à ce soir !, à la semaine prochaine ! Open-ended: à la prochaine ! (until next time!)
Bonne soirée, à demain !
Have a good evening, see you tomorrow!

categories.desc: Announcing you're leaving, and promising to stay in touch.
cards: Bon, je vais y aller.
Right, I'm going to head off.
The gentle signal that you're leaving. Bon warns that something's coming.
Bon, je vais y aller, il commence à être tard.
Right, I'm going to head off, it's getting late.
Faut que j'y aille.
I've got to go.
Spoken form of il faut que j'y aille. More urgent than je vais y aller.
Désolée, faut que j'y aille, mon bus arrive.
Sorry, I've got to go, my bus is coming.
Je te laisse.
I'll let you go.
Ends a call or a chat politely: I'll leave you to it. Formal: je vous laisse.
Bon, je te laisse, tu as du travail. Bisous !
Right, I'll let you go, you've got work. Love!
Je file !
I've got to dash!
Filer: to rush off. Same idea: je me sauve !
Je file, j'ai rendez-vous chez le dentiste.
I've got to dash, I've got a dentist's appointment.
On s'appelle !
Let's talk soon!
Literally ‘we'll call each other’. Casual, sometimes just politeness. Young slang: on se capte.
Super soirée ! On s'appelle cette semaine ?
Great evening! Shall we talk this week?
Tiens-moi au courant.
Keep me posted.
Asks for news later. Formal: tenez-moi au courant.
Bonne chance pour l'entretien, tiens-moi au courant !
Good luck with the interview, keep me posted!
